sheet_from: Data/Item/wwa.OZJ (16x16), red.OZJ (16x16), wwe.OZJ (64x64, red crystal facets in black) and wwe00.OZJ (64x32, a red glow), from MuMain with pipeline/decode_texture.py; 548 triangles over four meshes.
material_overrides_note: As the Devias staves' and the Divine Staff's: steel's own 0.2 mirrors the scene.
glow_note: ItemObjectAttribute (ZzzObject.cpp:5238-5241): `case MODEL_STAFF_OF_RESURRECTION: BlendMesh = -2; BlendMeshLight = sin(WorldTime*0.004)*0.3 + 0.7` -- every mesh drawn added and breathing (ZzzBMD.cpp:1509): the whole staff is a red glow. ZzzOpenData.cpp:1247's NoneBlendMesh on mesh 2 only keeps a levelled item's chrome pass off it (ZzzBMD.cpp:1425), as on the Chaos Dragon Axe; it was first read here as 'drawn solid', and wwe's black-backed cards stood as black squares on the staff (the user, 2026-10-03: 'staff of resurection needs work, black spots').
material_note: No baked material: MU draws all four meshes added (see glow_note), so the staff ships as glow parts on MU's raw sheets; the islands' materials go unused.
rig_note: Staff07.rig.json from export-rig --actions=all: seventeen bones, the five swirl cards' Box bones turning a full circle through the 4-key action 0 (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees), played always at held_loop (Figure::poseHeld). Its own rig, so asset.sh does not borrow the player's (the trap Staff06 records). Not here: what MuMain hangs on it held -- a warm BITMAP_SPARK and a BITMAP_SHINY+2 at its head, 145 units up the hand, and four spark particles thrown about it each frame (ZzzCharacter.cpp:10302-10318), client effects.
held_loop_from: MuMain plays the staff's action 0 always, at PLAYER_STOP_MALE's PlaySpeed 0.28 (ZzzOpenData.cpp:316-317) times 15 (ZzzCharacter.cpp:10125-10128): 4.2 keys a 25 Hz frame round a 4-key turn. Drawn at MU's 25 frames that is 0.2 of a key forward a frame -- 5 keys a second, a quarter turn a key: the five swirl cards on Box06, Box08, Box10, Box13 and Box16 spin about the head at 1.25 turns a second, which is what a player saw. `held_loop` is that, 1.25 turns a second, ours as a reading of the aliasing; the user, 2026-10-03: 'also i think that staff had some animations'.
